title: Dusting safety: footing, eyes and dust exposure
audience: Cleaners who dust shelves, high points and storage areas.
learningOutcomes: Choose eye protection and, where dust is heavy, a fitted dust mask before dusting.
Reach high points from a stable floor position without standing on furniture.
Identify loose or unstable items and report them rather than moving them.

instruction.heading: Eyes and breathing
instruction.body: Wear eye protection while dusting, because dust and debris can fall from above. When dust is heavy, such as in a storeroom that has not been cleaned for some time, add a dust mask. A mask protects only if it fits the face, so check the seal before you start.

instruction.heading: Footing and reaching
instruction.body: Do not stand on chairs, desks or furniture to reach. Use an extension tool and keep both feet on a stable floor. Watch for cables and items on the floor as you move between desks.

instruction.heading: Items on shelves
instruction.body: Look at what rests on the upper face of shelves and cabinets before you dust. Heavy or fragile items can fall when a shelf is touched. If an item looks unsafe to move, leave it, then ask for help or report it to the site contact.

instruction.heading: Recording near misses
instruction.body: If something nearly falls or you nearly lose your footing, record it with its location so the site can address it. A near miss recorded early is far cheaper to fix than an injury.

procedure: Check that eye protection is on, and add a fitted dust mask if dust is heavy.
Scan shelves and high points for loose or unstable items.
Reach with extension tools from a stable floor position.
Keep walkways clear of cables and items.
Report unstable items and record any near miss.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner notices a tall shelf with a loose box on top, and the dust on the shelf looks heavy.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not stand on anything. Put on a fitted dust mask, dust the shelf from the floor with an extension tool, and avoid the loose box. Report the box to the site contact for safe removal, and record the location.

commonErrors.error: Standing on a chair to reach a high shelf.
commonErrors.prevention: Use an extension tool from the floor.
Put eye protection on before leaving the storeroom.

commonErrors.error: Ignoring a loose item on a shelf.
commonErrors.prevention: Report it, and do not touch it.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Dust can be a health hazard. Choose a mask suited to the type of dust and check the site's controls.
Use a stable step only if the site supplies one that is designed for the purpose.
Report every near miss on the same day it happens.

qualityStandard: No one stands on furniture during dusting.
Eye protection is worn throughout the dusting task.
Loose items are reported, not moved.
documentationEvidence: Near misses and reports of unstable items recorded with their location.
summary: Wear eye protection, and add a fitted dust mask when dust is heavy.
Reach high points with an extension tool from a stable floor position.
Report unstable items and record near misses the same day.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the safer way to reach a high shelf?
options: An extension duster from a stable floor position
A chair with wheels, set close to the shelf
A desk drawer used as a step to reach it

knowledgeChecks.question: When is a dust mask needed?
A loose item sits on top of a shelf. What should you do?
options: Shake the shelf to test it and see if it moves
Report it to the site contact and avoid touching it
Move it onto a chair and dust the shelf below it
